name: WordPress Sitemap Intelligence Platform
tagline: Transform sitemaps into semantic knowledge graphs with DDD architecture
description: A comprehensive Next.js application that converts WordPress sitemap XML into interactive, multi-dimensional graph visualizations using Domain-Driven Design principles. Features include drill-down navigation, multiple view dimensions (section, category, date, asset-host), alternative layouts (hierarchical, radial, timeline, force-directed), and exportable diagrams.

domains.name: Semantic Graph Domain
domains.description: Core graph model with nodes (site, section, page, category, date, image, asset_host) and edges (contains, page, member, asset, related). Implements graph traversal, metadata extraction, and validation services.
features: Graph entity (aggregate root) with invariant enforcement
Node and Edge entities with rich metadata
NodeId value object with collision-resistant hashing
MetadataExtractionService (categories, dates, post types from URLs)

domains.name: Sitemap Ingestion Domain
domains.description: WordPress sitemap fetching, parsing, and merging. Handles sitemap.xml index files, recursive child sitemap fetching, and XML normalization.
features: Support for WordPress, custom sitemaps, and static XML

domains.name: Visualization & Navigation Domain
domains.description: Interactive graph rendering with multiple view dimensions, layout algorithms, search, filtering, and drill-down navigation. Supports Mermaid diagrams and Cytoscape.js interactive graphs.
features: ViewDimension value object (section, category, date, asset-host)
LayoutType value object (breadthfirst, radial, timeline, force)
FilterService (focus mode, depth limits, image visibility)

domains.name: Export & Rendering Domain
domains.description: Generate static Mermaid diagrams, SVG exports, and Cytoscape.js JSON for embedding. Support for sanitized outputs (remove placeholder nodes).

domains.name: Application Layer (Use Cases)
domains.description: CQRS implementation with queries (GetGraph, GetSubgraph, SearchNodes) and commands (IngestSitemap, BuildGraph, ExportGraph). Orchestrates domain services.
features: GetGraphQuery - Retrieve full graph or filtered subgraph
SearchNodesQuery - Full-text search across labels, URLs, metadata
IngestSitemapCommand - Fetch and process WordPress sitemap
BuildGraphCommand - Generate semantic graph from sitemap entries

domains.name: Infrastructure Layer (Adapters)
domains.description: Persistence (file system, in-memory for testing), HTTP clients (WordPress API), and rendering engines (Mermaid CLI, Cytoscape).

domains.name: Next.js Presentation Layer
domains.description: React Server Components, API routes, client components for interactivity. Tab-based UI (Mermaid vs Thought Map), controls, breadcrumbs, search.
features: Home page with Mermaid viewer (pan, zoom, export)
Thought Map page with Cytoscape.js canvas
SearchBox with debounced input and highlighting
Responsive layout with dark mode support

crew.assignment: Define bounded contexts, approve architecture decisions, ensure alignment with DDD principles
contributions: Defined 7 bounded contexts (graph, ingestion, visualization, export, application, infrastructure, presentation)
Established ubiquitous language (drill-down, breadcrumb, focus mode, placeholder node)
Approved clean architecture layers with dependency rules

crew.assignment: Set up Next.js project, configure build pipeline, implement repositories
contributions: Next.js 14 App Router setup with standalone output

crew.assignment: Implement domain services, application queries, React components
Design user interaction patterns, ensure accessibility, validate usability
contributions: Tab-based UI design (Mermaid vs Thought Map)

notes:
This project serves as both a production application AND a reference implementation for DDD architecture in Next.js. The codebase demonstrates clean architecture principles, bounded contexts, rich domain models, and comprehensive testing. It can be used as a template for future Alex AI projects requiring similar patterns.

Key architectural decisions:
1. Pure domain layer (no framework dependencies) for long-term maintainability
2. CQRS pattern for clear read/write separation
3. Repository pattern for data access abstraction
4. Value objects for type safety (NodeId, EdgeId, ViewDimension)
5. Application services for use case orchestration
6. Infrastructure adapters for external concerns

The project is intentionally over-engineered for a sitemap visualizer to showcase enterprise-grade patterns that can be applied to more complex domains (e-commerce, CRM, content management, etc.).
